1.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: When temperature and dew point converge within 4 F at sunset, radiation fog forms overnight.
core_mechanism_bullets: Upper Left: Air Temperature (F): Measured inside a shaded Stevenson screen at 2 meters above ground level.
Lower Left: Dew Point (Td): Measures exact atmospheric moisture; spread under 4 F signals saturation and fog.
Upper Right: Sea-Level Pressure: Standard sea-level pressure equals 1,013.25 mb (29.92 inHg or 14.7 psi).
Wind Shaft & Knot Feathers: Shaft points into the wind; short barb = 5 kt, long barb = 10 kt, pennant = 50 kt.
1.worked_field_example: At 62 F air temperature and 60 F dew point (a 2 F spread) under clear calm skies, expect dense ground fog by dawn.
1.counselor_tabletop_demo: Compare two NWS surface station plots and decode the temperature, dew point spread, sea-level pressure, and wind barb knots.
1.real_world_connection_box: NOAA NWS JetStream Field Standard: When temperature and dew point converge within 4 F at sunset, radiation fog forms overnight.
1.grounded_citation_label: Verified: Scouting America Pamphlet + NOAA NWS JetStream
1.bespoke_visual_caption: NOAA surface station plot decoder showing temperature, dew point depression, sea-level pressure in millibars, and wind speed barbs in knots.

primary_source_citation.title: NOAA National Severe Storms Lab Technical Reference: Supercell Charge Separation, Hail Growth & 30/30 Safety

2.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Five seconds from lightning flash to thunder equals one mile, so seek shelter at thirty seconds or less.
core_mechanism_bullets: Stage 1: Condensation Nucleus (0.0002 mm): Water vapor condenses onto microscopic dust and sea-salt aerosols above lifting level.
Stage 2: Bergeron Raindrop Growth (2.0 mm): One 2.0 mm raindrop combines roughly 1,000,000 microscopic cloud droplets.
Stage 3: Graupel-Ice Charge Split: Supercooled water and ice crystal collisions build 100-million-volt potential.
Stage 4: Severe Updraft Hail (>55 mph): 25 mm quarter-size hail requires sustained updraft speeds exceeding 55 mph.
2.worked_field_example: A fifteen-second flash-to-bang count means the lightning strike is three miles away and already within immediate shelter range.
2.counselor_tabletop_demo: Use a stopwatch to time a simulated flash-to-bang interval and divide the seconds by five to calculate storm distance in miles.
2.real_world_connection_box: NOAA National Severe Storms Lab Standard: Five seconds from lightning flash to thunder equals one mile, so seek shelter at thirty seconds or less. Strong thunderstorm updrafts cycle ice pellets across the freezing level to build concentric hailstone layers.
2.grounded_citation_label: Verified: Scouting America Pamphlet + NOAA National Severe Storms Lab
2.bespoke_visual_caption: Vertical supercell cutaway showing warm updrafts, cool downdrafts, hailstone cycling above the freezing line, and cloud-to-ground lightning.

4.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: A Severe Weather Watch means atmospheric ingredients are present so patrols should prepare early.
core_mechanism_bullets: Tier 1: NWS Forecast Discussion (48 Hr): Check local NWS Weather Forecast Office hourly graph before departing on any campout.
Tier 2: Severe Weather WATCH: Atmospheric ingredients are present across a multi-county zone; review shelter plan and gear.
Tier 3: Severe Weather WARNING: Doppler radar or spotters confirm imminent hazard; move immediately to designated hard shelter.
Tier 4: Backcountry Execution: Turn Around Dont Drown (6 in moving water knocks down an adult); wait 30 min after last thunder.
4.worked_field_example: When a Tornado Watch upgrades to a Tornado Warning at camp, move patrols immediately from tents to a reinforced masonry building.

4.real_world_connection_box: NOAA Storm Prediction Center Field Standard: A Severe Weather Watch means atmospheric ingredients are present so patrols should prepare early. A Severe Weather Warning means hazardous weather is active on radar and requires immediate shelter.

primary_source_citation.title: NOAA Cooperative Observer Program Technical Reference: Four Field Weather Instruments & Calibration Principles

7.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Funneling a 4-inch collector into a 1.26-inch cylinder magnifies rainfall depth tenfold for 0.01-inch precision.
core_mechanism_bullets: Wind Vane (True North): Larger tail fin catches wind so pointer faces directly into incoming airflow; align with magnetic declination.
4-Cup Anemometer (RPM): Count colored-cup revolutions in 60 seconds and multiply by circumference and calibration factor.
10:1 Magnifying Rain Gauge: Narrow inner measuring tube expands vertical water height 10x so 0.01 inch is easy to read.
Hair Hygrometer (Humidity): Human hair lengthens by 2.5 percent as relative humidity rises from 0 percent to 100 percent.
7.worked_field_example: Collecting 2.50 inches of water inside a 10x magnified inner measuring tube records exactly 0.25 inches of actual rainfall.
7.counselor_tabletop_demo: Pour 10 milliliters of water through a 4-inch funnel into a narrow graduated tube to demonstrate 10x depth magnification.
7.real_world_connection_box: NOAA Cooperative Observer Program Standard: Funneling a 4-inch collector into a 1.26-inch cylinder magnifies rainfall depth tenfold for 0.01-inch precision.
7.grounded_citation_label: Verified: Scouting America Pamphlet + NOAA Cooperative Observer Program
7.bespoke_visual_caption: Handcrafted meteorological instruments showing a wind vane, four-cup anemometer, graduated rain collector, and wet-and-dry-bulb psychrometer.
